cases.sentence: В один из ___, в конце марта, когда уже на земле не было снега и в больничном саду пели скворцы, доктор вышел проводить до ворот своего приятеля почтмейстера.
cases.explain: «весенних вечеров» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On a spring evening towards the end of March, when there was no snow left on the ground and the starlings were singing in the hospital garden, the doctor went out to see his friend the postmaster as far as the gate. At that very moment the Jew Moiseika, returning with his booty, came into the yard. He had no cap on, and his bare feet were thrust into goloshes; in his hand he had a little bag of coppers.

cases.sentence: Он был без шапки и в ___ на босую ногу и в руках держал небольшой мешочек с милостыней.

cases.sentence: «Как это нехорошо, – подумал он, глядя на его ___ с красными тощими щиколками. – Ведь мокро».
cases.explain: «босые ноги» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “How bad that is!” he thought, looking at the Jew’s bare feet with their thin red ankles. “Why, it’s wet.”

cases.sentence: «Как это нехорошо, – подумал он, глядя на его босые ноги с красными ___. – Ведь мокро».
cases.explain: «тощими щиколками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “How bad that is!” he thought, looking at the Jew’s bare feet with their thin red ankles. “Why, it’s wet.”

cases.sentence: ___! – взвизгнул он и в исступлении, какого никогда еще не видели в палате, топнул ногой. – Убить эту гадину!
cases.explain: «Проклятая гадина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The doctor has come!” he shouted, and broke into a laugh. “At last! Gentlemen, I congratulate you. The doctor is honouring us with a visit! Cursed reptile!” he shrieked, and stamped in a frenzy such as had never been seen in the ward before. “Kill the reptile! No, killing’s too good. Drown him in the midden-pit!”

cases.sentence: – За что? – крикнул Иван Дмитрич, подходя к нему с ___ и судорожно запахиваясь в халат. – За что?
cases.explain: «угрожающим видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “What for?” shouted Ivan Dmitritch, going up to him with a menacing air and convulsively wrapping himself in his dressing-gown. “What for? Thief!” he said with a look of repulsion, moving his lips as though he would spit at him. “Quack! hangman!”

cases.sentence: Вы, фельдшер, смотритель и вся ваша больничная сволочь в ___ неизмеримо ниже каждого из нас, почему же мы сидим, а вы нет?
cases.explain: «нравственном отношении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes, I am ill. But you know dozens, hundreds of madmen are walking about in freedom because your ignorance is incapable of distinguishing them from the sane. Why am I and these poor wretches to be shut up here like scapegoats for all the rest? You, your assistant, the superintendent, and all your hospital rabble, are immeasurably inferior to every one of us morally; why then are we shut up and you not? Where’s the logic of it?”

cases.sentence: – ___ и логика тут ни при чем.
cases.explain: «Нравственное отношение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Morality and logic don’t come in, it all depends on chance. If anyone is shut up he has to stay, and if anyone is not shut up he can walk about, that’s all. There is neither morality nor logic in my being a doctor and your being a mental patient, there is nothing but idle chance.”

cases.sentence: Голос Ивана Дмитрича и его молодое ___ с гримасами понравились Андрею Ефимычу.
cases.explain: «умное лицо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Andrey Yefimitch liked Ivan Dmitritch’s voice and his intelligent young face with its grimaces. He longed to be kind to the young man and soothe him; he sat down on the bed beside him, thought, and said:

cases.sentence: Ему захотелось приласкать ___ и успокоить его.
cases.explain: «молодого человека» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Andrey Yefimitch liked Ivan Dmitritch’s voice and his intelligent young face with its grimaces. He longed to be kind to the young man and soothe him; he sat down on the bed beside him, thought, and said:

cases.sentence: Когда общество ограждает себя от преступников, психических больных и вообще ___, то оно непобедимо.
cases.explain: «неудобных людей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “You ask me what to do. The very best thing in your position would be to run away. But, unhappily, that is useless. You would be taken up. When society protects itself from the criminal, mentally deranged, or otherwise inconvenient people, it is invincible. There is only one thing left for you: to resign yourself to the thought that your presence here is inevitable.”

cases.sentence: – Вы шутите, – сказал он, щуря глаза. – Таким господам, как вы и ваш помощник Никита, нет никакого дела до будущего, но можете быть уверены, ___, настанут лучшие времена!
cases.explain: «милостивый государь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You are jesting,” he said, screwing up his eyes. “Such gentlemen as you and your assistant Nikita have nothing to do with the future, but you may be sure, sir, better days will come! I may express myself cheaply, you may laugh, but the dawn of a new life is at hand; truth and justice will triumph, and—our turn will come! I shall not live to see it, I shall perish, but some people’s great-grandsons will see it. I greet them with all my heart and rejoice, rejoice with them! Onward! God be your help, friends!”

cases.sentence: Иван Дмитрич с ___ поднялся и, протягивая руки к окну, продолжал с волнением в голосе:
cases.explain: «блестящими глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: With shining eyes Ivan Dmitritch got up, and stretching his hands towards the window, went on with emotion in his voice:

cases.sentence: Какая бы ___ ни освещала вашу жизнь, всё же в конце концов вас заколотят в гроб и бросят в яму.
cases.explain: «великоепная заря» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I see no particular reason to rejoice,” said Andrey Yefimitch, who thought Ivan Dmitritch’s movement theatrical, though he was delighted by it. “Prisons and madhouses there will not be, and truth, as you have just expressed it, will triumph; but the reality of things, you know, will not change, the laws of nature will still remain the same. People will suffer pain, grow old, and die just as they do now. However magnificent a dawn lighted up your life, you would yet in the end be nailed up in a coffin and thrown into a hole.”

cases.sentence: А я глубоко верю, что если нет бессмертия, то его рано или поздно изобретет великий ___.
cases.explain: «человеческий ум» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You don’t believe in it, but I do. Somebody in Dostoevsky or Voltaire said that if there had not been a God men would have invented him. And I firmly believe that if there is no immortality the great intellect of man will sooner or later invent it.”

cases.sentence: Свободное и глубокое мышление, которое стремится к уразумению жизни, и полное презрение к ___ мира – вот два блага, выше которых никогда не знал человек.
cases.explain: «глупой суете» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “You are a reflecting and a thoughtful man. In any surroundings you can find tranquillity in yourself. Free and deep thinking which strives for the comprehension of life, and complete contempt for the foolish bustle of the world—those are two blessings beyond any that man has ever known. And you can possess them even though you lived behind threefold bars. Diogenes lived in a tub, yet he was happier than all the kings of the earth.”

cases.sentence: Впрочем, приехал недавно ___ Хоботов.
cases.explain: «молодой врач» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, in the town it is appallingly dull. … There’s no one to say a word to, no one to listen to. There are no new people. A young doctor called Hobotov has come here recently.”

cases.sentence: – Да, не ___.
cases.explain: «культурный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, he is a man of no culture. It’s strange, you know. … Judging by every sign, there is no intellectual stagnation in our capital cities; there is a movement—so there must be real people there too; but for some reason they always send us such men as I would rather not see. It’s an unlucky town!”

cases.sentence: Судя по всему, в наших столицах нет умственного застоя, есть движение, – значит, должны быть там и ___, но почему-то всякий раз оттуда присылают к нам таких людей, что не глядел бы.

It’s an unlucky town!”

cases.sentence: – Да, ___! – вздохнул Иван Дмитрич и засмеялся. – А вообще как?
cases.explain: «несчастный город» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, it is an unlucky town,” sighed Ivan Dmitritch, and he laughed. “And how are things in general? What are they writing in the papers and reviews?”

cases.sentence: «Какой приятный ___! – думал Андрей Ефимыч, идя к себе на квартиру. – За всё время, пока я тут живу, это, кажется, первый, с которым можно поговорить.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What an agreeable young man!” thought Andrey Yefimitch, going back to his flat. “In all the years I have been living here I do believe he is the first I have met with whom one can talk. He is capable of reasoning and is interested in just the right things.”
